reason: Seawater can enter seafloor fractures to begin the circulation loop.
expectation: Seawater will flow down into the fractured rock.

effect: The accumulating early sea has no available combination, so I will try the mineral-bearing seawater instead.
reaction: The distinction between the two sea items was not obvious.
reason: The mineral-bearing seawater may enter the open fractures and start the circulation loop.
expectation: Seawater will enter the fractured seafloor.

effect: Mineral-bearing seawater enters the crust, starting the circulation loop.
reaction: The seawater distinction is clearer now.
reason: Water entering the crust should heat as it approaches hot rock.
expectation: The circulating seawater will heat up underground.

effect: The seawater is now heated inside the crust; it still needs a route back to the sea.
reaction: The role of pressure in keeping hot fluid underground is interesting.
reason: The next step in the circulation loop is not yet obvious, so I will check what the heated water can interact with.
expectation: The inspection will identify an available next step toward a vent.

effect: The heated water reacted with buried rock, producing mineral-bearing hydrothermal fluid; the next step is to return it to the sea.
reaction: It was useful to see that heating and water–rock reactions are separate steps.
reason: I expect the hot fluid to rise through seafloor fractures toward the vent.
expectation: The hydrothermal fluid will rise through the fractures toward the sea.

effect: The mineral-bearing fluid is rising through fractures toward the seafloor.
reaction: The separate entry and return paths make the circulation loop clearer.
reason: The returning hot fluid should meet cooler seawater at the vent.
expectation: The fluid will emerge into the sea and cool, potentially depositing minerals.

effect: Mixing with cooler seawater caused minerals to precipitate at a vent; the heated-water return goal may still need a separate step.
reaction: It is satisfying to see dissolved material become a solid deposit.
reason: I will check how the precipitating minerals can build the vent deposit.
expectation: The inspection will reveal what can help form the deposit.

effect: The precipitated minerals built a deposit around the outlet, completing the vent-deposit goal. Heated water still needs to return to the sea.
reaction: The modest deposit is a useful alternative to assuming every vent forms a tall chimney.
reason: The returning fluid may have another available interaction that completes the circulation loop.
expectation: The inspection will reveal how to return the heated water to the sea.

effect: The returning fluid mixed into the sea as a hydrothermal plume, completing the circulation goal and the chapter.
reaction: The distinction between suspended mineral particles and smoke was useful.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following the heated water’s reaction with rock through to mineral precipitation made the vent process clear, especially the distinction between heating and chemical exchange.

leastWorthwhile.text: The first attempt was frustrating: the accumulating sea could not combine with fractures, although the other sea item could.

surprise.text: The plume’s visible material is suspended minerals, not smoke; the deposit also need not become a towering chimney.

arbitrary.text: The distinction between the two sea items felt arbitrary at first: one began the circulation loop, while the other was used to complete it.

continue.text: Yes. I would continue for another chapter if it offered similarly concrete connections between physical processes and visible results.
